name: Software Engineer (Generalist)
description: Entry-level generalist software engineer for product-company interviews: core CS, data structures, design and clean code.

skills.name: Data Structures & Complexity
skills.description: Core structures and Big-O reasoning: arrays, hash maps, trees, graphs, heaps, sorting and searching.

L1: Names the exact data structures and algorithms used in the project
States which parts they personally built versus a teammate, a tutorial or a library
L2: Explains why a hash map lookup is O(1) on average and when it degrades
Explains the time and space cost of a sort they used
Explains when a heap or balanced tree beats an array
L3: Explains when they would NOT use the structure they picked and what breaks
Defends a choice between two structures with concrete costs for their input size

skills.name: Operating Systems & Concurrency
skills.description: Processes, threads, scheduling, memory, locks and deadlocks.

L1: Names the exact concurrency primitives and where they were used used in the project
States which parts they personally built versus a teammate, a tutorial or a library
L2: Explains the difference between a process and a thread
Explains how a race condition arises and how a lock prevents it
Explains the four conditions for deadlock
L3: Explains when they would NOT use a lock or extra threads, and the cost
Defends a concurrency approach against a concrete alternative with a real cost of each

skills.name: Databases
skills.description: Relational modelling, joins, indexes, transactions and query performance.

L1: Names the exact tables, queries and schema used in the project
States which parts they personally built versus a teammate, a tutorial or a library
L2: Explains what an index speeds up and what it costs on writes
Explains the difference between INNER and LEFT JOIN with an example
Explains what a transaction guarantees (atomicity, isolation) and a bug it prevents
L3: Explains when they would denormalize or NOT add an index, and the trade-off
Defends SQL vs a document store for their data with a real cost of each
Explains how they found and fixed a slow query (EXPLAIN, index, rewrite)

skills.name: Computer Networks
skills.description: TCP vs UDP, HTTP, DNS, TLS and what happens when a page loads.

L1: Names the exact protocols used in the project used in the project
States which parts they personally built versus a teammate, a tutorial or a library
L2: Explains TCP vs UDP and when each fits
Explains what happens from typing a URL to a page loading
Explains what TLS protects and what it does not
L3: Explains when they would NOT use TCP or HTTP for a feature
Defends a protocol choice against a concrete alternative with a real cost of each

skills.name: OOP & Clean Code
skills.description: Object-oriented design, SOLID, design patterns and readable, testable code.

L1: Names the exact classes, patterns and responsibilities used in the project
States which parts they personally built versus a teammate, a tutorial or a library
L2: Explains composition vs inheritance with an example from their code
Explains one SOLID principle and a bug it prevents
Explains a design pattern they used and the problem it solved
L3: Explains when they would NOT apply a pattern and the over-engineering cost
Defends a design against a concrete alternative with a real cost of each

skills.name: System Design Basics
skills.description: Scaling a service: caching, queues, load balancing, replication, consistency and failure.

L1: Names the exact components of the system (cache, queue, database) and what each did used in the project
States which parts they personally built versus a teammate, a tutorial or a library
L2: Explains what a cache invalidation problem looks like and one strategy to handle it
Explains why a queue decouples producers from consumers and what happens when it backs up
Explains the difference between vertical and horizontal scaling
L3: Explains when they would NOT add a cache, queue or microservice, and the cost they avoid
Defends a consistency vs availability choice for a concrete feature, naming what a user would see on failure

skills.name: Git & Collaboration
skills.description: Version control workflow: branching, merging, rebasing, pull requests, and recovering from mistakes.

L1: Names the exact git commands and branching workflow used in the project
States which parts they personally built versus a teammate, a tutorial or a library
L2: Explains the difference between merge and rebase and what each does to history
Explains how to resolve a merge conflict step by step
Explains how revert differs from reset
L3: Explains when they would NOT rebase (shared branches) and the cost of rewriting history
Defends a branching strategy (trunk-based vs feature branches) against the alternative for a team of their size
